title: The Odyssey
subtitle: The Long Way Home
attribution: An original abridged adaptation of Homer’s Odyssey
description: A song, a choice, a hunger: the sea asks for more than courage.
intro: Some dangers sound like exactly what we want.
ending: The telling was finished. Now someone else would carry him home.
stageLabel: A pixel art retelling of the Odyssey

adaptationSource.title: Homer, Odyssey, Books XII–XIII
adaptationSource.note: Original abridged English narration and dialogue. Events are condensed for quiet episodic reading. Ritual sacrifice and deaths are represented without gore. The final conflict of Book XXIV is condensed to Athena intervening before renewed bloodshed.

steps.text: After burying Elpenor, the men followed the path back to their ship. Circe’s warnings guided their next journey.
Before reaching the Sirens, Odysseus explained the plan. His men would block their ears with wax and tie him to the mast.

transition.reason: Establish the next scene with its existing cast

steps.text: The ropes held Odysseus aboard. Eurylochus, Polites and the other sailors could not hear the dangerous song through the wax.
With wax in their ears, the crew rowed past the Sirens. Odysseus stood tied to the mast, listening.
The voices offered him the story of Troy—everything he had suffered, made whole and understood.
“Untie me. Let me hear.”
Eurylochus and Polites could not hear him through the wax. Odysseus had told them to keep rowing, even if he begged to stop.
They pulled the oars until the voices fell behind. Only then did they free him.
He looked back once. The song was gone, but the wanting had not left him yet.

steps.text: After the Sirens, the ship reached a narrow strait. On one side, Charybdis pulled the water into a huge whirlpool.
On the other side lived Scylla, a monster with six heads. The ship had to pass between these two dangers.
Odysseus chose the cliff side. Circe had told him that the whirlpool could swallow the whole ship.
“Keep rowing. Do not stop here.”
Scylla snatched six of the other sailors from the deck. Odysseus, Eurylochus and Polites survived and kept the ship moving.
The men who remained kept rowing. Their captain had chosen a way through, but could not call it a victory.
He had heard his companions call his name. That was the sound he carried beyond the strait.
The crew stepped ashore and followed the sandy path into a meadow. Their ship stayed at the landing.

steps.text: After escaping the strait, the tired crew needed to rest. They reached an island where Helios’s cattle grazed.
Odysseus remembered Tiresias’s warning about the Sun’s cattle. He made every sailor promise not to hurt them.
“These animals are not ours to take.”
Strong winds kept them from sailing away for many days. Their stored food ran out, and the hungry men began looking at the cattle.
While Odysseus slept, Eurylochus and Polites went toward the herd. They wanted food, although they knew the warning.
“Better to face the gods than die here without trying.”
They killed a sacred cow and made a sacrifice. The meal quieted their hunger; it did not undo the choice.
Odysseus woke beside the embers. The wind had changed, but the warning remained.
When the wind eased, the men returned down the path. Odysseus was troubled by what they had done, but they were ready to sail.

steps.text: Helios saw that his cattle had been killed. He asked Zeus, the ruler of the gods, to punish the sailors.
A storm caught the ship after they left the island. The wind rose against them, and the daylight darkened.

steps.text: Zeus’s thunderbolt broke the ship. The sea took every remaining companion. Eurylochus and Polites would never see their homes.
Odysseus held to wreckage. There was no crew left to call to, no ship left to guide.
The current dragged him through the dark water. He kept his hold on the broken timber.
For nine more days, the water carried him. The journey had become one man refusing to let go.
For nine days there was only water. He could not know what shore would find him.

calypso.zone: Left foliage beside the lower sandy path

steps.text: The sea washed Odysseus onto Calypso’s island. She found him on the shore and cared for him. Days there became years.
That was where this telling began: a man on a shore, still looking toward a home he could not see.
His memories had reached the island where our story began. Later came his raft, the storm and Nausicaa’s help.

transition.reason: Return from the remembered island to the listening hall

steps.text: Back in Alcinous’s hall, the telling of the past was over. The king, queen and singer were still listening to Odysseus.
“I have brought back only myself.”
“Then we will bring you the rest of the way.”
Alcinous’s people were called the Phaeacians. The king would send a fresh crew to take Odysseus from Scheria to Ithaca.
This time, he would not have to watch the helm. Another crew would carry him while he slept.
